PROSE:
Rhea hit the cold paved stone of the outskirts, tumbling shoulder-over-hip until friction finally arrested her momentum. Behind her, the massive firewall of deletion code snapped shut with a sound like a guillotine severing a power line. She lay flat on her back on the high ridge, gasping for breath, staring up at a sky that no longer looked like an ash-choked tutorial. It was a crisp, oppressive slate-gray, perfectly uniform and entirely synthetic. 

[Status Alert: Stamina is currently 0/150.]
[Status Effect: Exhaustion (Severe) remains active. Natural stamina regeneration halted. Further physical exertion will incur direct HP penalties.]

The math was absolute. Zero stamina didn't mean she was just tired. It meant the System had physically disconnected the concept of kinetic energy from her musculature. Her arms weighed a thousand pounds. Her lungs heaved, pulling in air that tasted sharply of ozone and polished concrete, but the oxygen did nothing to fuel her cells. She was a biological machine running on a completely empty tank, kept alive only by the base-level grace of her remaining hit points. 

To her left, a heavy metallic clatter announced Vance’s arrival. He had been spat out of the breach a second before her, and he currently looked like a man who had been fed through a meat grinder and reassembled by a blind mechanic. He was on his hands and knees, coughing violently, his blistered hands maintaining a death grip on his trusted weapon. 

"Status," Rhea croaked, the word scraping out of her throat like sandpaper.

Vance spat a glob of blood onto the pristine stone. "Alive," he grunted, shifting his weight and immediately wincing. "Barely. The system is currently informing me that my ribs are mathematically compromised."

[Vance Harrow - Status Check]
[Active Effect: Heavy Blunt-Force Trauma. Mobility reduced. Pain receptors operating at maximum threshold.]

He leveraged the length of the rebar against the ground, using it as a crutch to push himself into a sitting position. The metal groaned under his weight. It was bent at a thirty-degree angle near the top, the result of smashing through a collapsing support beam during their frantic escape from the inner office. 

"Durability is sitting at fifty-two percent," Vance muttered, eyeing the bent iron with profound disgust. "A few more solid hits and it’s going to shatter into untaxed scrap. I’ve got the restorative consumables stowed in my right cargo pocket, but I’m saving them. If I pop them now, the system might flag the healing as a taxable event in a new zone. I don't trust the local economy yet."

"Smart," Rhea whispered. She didn't have the energy to nod. 

A few yards away, a pathetic whirring sound drew their attention. Unit 734 had survived the breach, but 'survived' was a generous term. The drone’s smoking chassis was a mangled mess of scorched brass and exposed copper wiring. Plumes of acrid black smoke vented continuously from its primary cooling ports, smelling strongly of burning plastic and fried logic boards. 

[Diagnostic: Unit 734]
[Chassis Integrity: 28%]
[Status: Critical System Failure Imminent.]

"Diagnostic," the drone buzzed, its voice synthesizer skipping an octave. "Chassis integrity at twenty-eight percent. Warning. Critical system failure imminent. Structural collapse projected in... calculating... calculating..."

"Don't calculate," Rhea said, forcing herself to roll onto her side. The movement cost her a point of HP, a tiny red [-1] floating up from her shoulder, but she needed to see the drone. "Just power down non-essential subroutines. Keep your core logic intact. You're our only map of this place."

"Query," Unit 734 clicked, its single optical lens flickering erratically. "Define 'this place'. We have exited the designated tutorial parameters. We are currently undocumented entities in an unregistered zone. We are anomalies."

Rhea managed to prop herself up on her left elbow. Her singed arm hair brushed against the cold stone. Her left hand was empty, but she could feel the reassuring weight of her inventory in her left blazer pocket. The raw data packet. The null-value token. The Mercy Cache coordinates. They were all there, safely tucked away in the fabric. 

But it was her right hand that held the real prize. 

Her fingers were curled tightly around the Administrative Residue Token. It was heavy, far heavier than a piece of digital loot had any right to be. It pulsed with a slow, rhythmic blue light, casting long, eerie shadows across the paved stone of the ridge. The token wasn't just an item; it was a severed piece of the overseer's authority. It was a master key to a lock they hadn't even found yet. 

"We aren't anomalies," Rhea said, her voice gaining a fraction of its usual sharp edge. "We're auditors."

She forced herself to look back over her shoulder. The edge of the high ridge dropped off into a sheer cliff of smooth, featureless obsidian. Beyond the cliff was the frontier zone—or rather, where the frontier zone used to be. 

The deletion wave was a terrifying thing to behold. It wasn't an explosion. It wasn't a fire. It was a localized cessation of reality. A massive, towering wall of raw, red code was slowly sweeping across the ash wastes. Where it touched the petrified trees, the trees simply ceased to exist, their polygons dissolving into a flurry of red numbers before winking out completely. The ruined tollbooth, the maintenance trenches, the administrative sanctum—all of it was being scrubbed from the Ledger's memory banks. The overseer was dead, his account in catastrophic default, and the system was aggressively cleaning up the mess. 

"Good riddance," Vance muttered, leaning heavily on his rebar. "Place was a rigged casino anyway."

"It wasn't a casino," Rhea corrected, watching the red wall consume the last of the ash dunes. "A casino implies a statistical chance of winning. That was a slaughterhouse. We just managed to break the bolt gun."

She turned her gaze away from the destruction and looked forward. 

If the frontier zone had been a slaughterhouse, the Civic Layer was a sprawling, infinite corporate empire. 

The high ridge they were perched on overlooked a valley that defied human comprehension. It was a city, but not one built for people. It was a city built for ledgers, for transactions, for the endless, grinding bureaucracy of the System. Monolithic spires of black glass and polished steel pierced the artificial clouds. The architecture was aggressive, all sharp angles and brutalist geometry, designed to make the observer feel small, insignificant, and entirely replaceable. 

Instead of roads, massive conduits of glowing blue and gold data streamed between the buildings, carrying unimaginable volumes of systemic wealth. The air hummed with a low, pervasive vibration—the sound of a billion micro-transactions happening simultaneously. 

"Well," Vance said, his voice quiet, stripped of its usual cynical armor. "That's... big."

"It is the institutional core," Unit 734 buzzed, its optical lens struggling to focus on the sprawling metropolis. "The Civic Layer. Population: Unquantifiable. Threat Level: Absolute. We do not have the proper zoning permits to exist here. We do not have the required tax brackets. We are going to be repossessed."

"Let them try," Rhea said. 

She looked down at the Administrative Residue Token in her right hand. The blue light it emitted seemed to harmonize with the distant glow of the data streams below. She had the proof of the skim. She had the coordinates to the Mercy Cache. And she had an illicit access token that the system hadn't figured out how to delete yet. 

The math of the tutorial had been about surviving the physical environment. The math of the Civic Layer was going to be about surviving the economy. And Rhea Mercer was an accountant. 

[Warning: Audit Compliance (Red-Tier) marker is still active.]
[Hostile Environment Marker is still active.]

The system hadn't forgotten about them. The local node had crashed, but the overarching Ledger was vast, and it was already attempting to reconcile the discrepancy they represented. 

Rhea gripped the token tighter. The zero stamina was agonizing, a constant, crushing weight on her chest, but the adrenaline of the exploit was still humming in her veins. They had done the impossible. They had forced a catastrophic default on a System administrator. They had broken the rules and survived the resulting deletion wave. 

"Vance," Rhea said, her eyes locked on the towering spires of the city. "How much durability do you really have left in that rebar?"

Vance patted the iron shaft. "Fifty-two percent. Why? You planning on hitting a building?"

"No," Rhea said, a grim smile touching the corners of her mouth. "But we're going to need to break a few windows."

As she spoke the words, the Administrative Residue Token flared with a sudden, blinding intensity. The physical weight of the item vanished, dissolving into a stream of pure, liquid light that sank directly into the pores of her right hand. 

Rhea gasped, dropping her hand as the light surged up her arm, burning cold and sharp. It didn't deal damage. It didn't trigger a stamina penalty. Instead, it bypassed her physical stats entirely, interfacing directly with her character continuity state. 

The air in front of her shattered. 

Not a physical break, but a digital one. A massive, stark blue system window manifested, hovering in the space between the high ridge and the sprawling city. It didn't look like the crude, functional prompts of the frontier zone. This window was elegant, framed in gold, with text that seemed to burn with an authoritative finality. 

The system had finally caught up. It had processed the breach, analyzed the anomaly, and recognized the illicit token now permanently bound to her ledger. 

Rhea stared at the floating blue rectangle, the reflection of the text glowing in her exhausted eyes. The sheer scale of the institutional city loomed in the background, a vast machine waiting to grind them into dust. But for this one, singular moment, the machine was forced to acknowledge her.

[Entity Migration Detected. Origin: Deleted Node. Destination: Civic Layer.]

[Token Registration]
[Administrative Residue Token (Illicit) recognized. Access privileges temporarily granted under Clause 44-B (Disputed Authority).]

[Civic Layer Welcome]
[Welcome to the Civic Layer, Auditor. Your presence is highly irregular. Your survival is statistically anomalous. Your impending bankruptcy is guaranteed.]
